title: Early ambitions and the Doctor's Band in high school
summary: Baron says he loved music from high school and played with a local band of dentists and lawyers who took him in; he was a rebel about curfews.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive, on campus. I’m very pleased to have multi-instrumentalist Art Baron with me today. I was reading through your resume trying to find out a name of someone you haven’t played with.
I’ve been a very lucky guy.
Yeah. Easier to find out who you haven’t — when you were 17 let’s say, did you have those kinds of aspirations, to just be —

Since I was like a senior or a junior in high school. You know I was having so much fun in music. I did everything I could. Like I was in high school, and there was a local group of musicians, The Doctor’s Band, and they met like once every two weeks or so. Dentists, lawyers, some of them had gone out with territory bands, and some of them were great. There was a dentist there that sounded like Marshall Royal on lead alto. His name was Dr. Culshack. He laid that down man. And these guys took me in, and I just had the greatest time. And I was a rebel. I was like a middle child and like I would go to these rehearsals and they’d have a jam session sometimes afterwards and I got home like at twelve, when they said be home at eleven, so they took the car away for a week or two. I’d go out and do it again. I kept just doing it. I think they finally gave up on me. But it was just what I loved doing, you know. When I was a kid, in the fifth or sixth grade, I was pretty good in most subjects, at that time anyway. But I didn’t have that identity of like sports or this or that. But I went through my first year of playing music, and I almost quit trombone. And the second year all of a sudden I just took to it, and I just boom. You know I was practicing hours a day, and loving it. I did everything I could musical.
